analyst.summary: Cochin Shipyard's FY26 numbers confirm the quant model's read: revenue grew just 4.2% (Rs 5,022cr vs Rs 4,820cr, per internal PIT quarterly data), a sharp step-down from the 28.5% 3-year CAGR and a miss against management's own 14-15% FY26 growth guidance, with quarterly operating margins swinging violently (23% to 7% to 14% to 21% across FY26's four quarters) on percentage-of-completion project-mix timing. The Sep-25 quarter is a genuine earnings-quality flag: net profit fell 43% YoY as core shipbuilding operations generated barely Rs 22.6cr of pre-tax profit, with schedule-contingent SBFAP subsidy accrual and treasury income supplying roughly 85% of that quarter's reported PBT. At ~51-52x trailing earnings the stock is the richest of the three listed defence shipyards despite having by far the weakest ROE (13.6% vs Mazagon Dock's ~37% and GRSE's ~40%), and Kotak has moved to an explicit Sell (target Rs 830, -48%) citing a two-year drought in major defence order wins and a medium-term pipeline it cut to Rs 30,000cr from Rs 50,000cr. Set against that, IAC-2 -- the second aircraft carrier, biddable only by Cochin Shipyard -- remains a real, un-calendarable catalyst (Acceptance of Necessity targeted late 2026, Cabinet Committee on Security sign-off still pending) that could reprice the order book overnight, and brokerage targets are unusually dispersed (Rs 830 to Rs 2,175) after the stock's own ~30% 12-month de-rating. Net call: Sell, but by a narrower margin than the headline multiple alone would suggest, given the live optionality and wide sell-side disagreement.
